dem-liggghts-auger-short.method: smoke-test rerun of PR #180 rig auger case rig_t27p5_r60: 0.12 s settle + 0.25 rev, dry vs SJKR cohesion
dem-liggghts-auger-short.notes: Geometry/inputs regenerated with the #180 branch's geometry.py + run_case.py (STL meshes, np=1). PR #180 reported 12 mg in the first quarter revolution for this case. The cohesive run was paused (SIGSTOP) from 02:26:14 to 02:57:24 UTC when the shared runner was oversubscribed; its active wall time is 2352 s elapsed minus 1870 s paused = 482 s (370 s CPU).

dem-liggghts-aor.method: angle of repose, poured heap on a fixed 12 mm base (ISO 4324 style, reduced scale)
dem-liggghts-aor.notes: Real-size salt grains (no coarse-graining), E reduced to 2e5 Pa. Profile-fit angle = slope of the sector-averaged heap surface for 1.0 < r < 5.2 mm; apex angle = atan(apex height / base radius) as in ISO 4324.

dem-liggghts-drum.method: rotating drum, 16 mm diameter, 2.55 mm periodic slice, 20 rpm (Froude 0.0036)
dem-liggghts-drum.notes: Angle = slope of a line fitted to the top of the bed over the central 60 % of the drum width, per 0.02 s dump, averaged over the window. Rough wall: frozen 0.3 mm spheres rotated with fix move rotate. Cohesive run: major avalanches from 62.0 deg (t=0.59 s) to 25.3 deg (0.71 s) and from 53.6 deg (1.07 s) into a slump at 1.11-1.19 s; fitted angles of 13-22 deg during the slump are artifacts (surface not straight). Local extrema lists include small wiggles.

dem-liggghts-hall.method: Hall (2.54 mm) and Carney (5.08 mm) 60-degree funnel discharge, reduced funnel height
dem-liggghts-hall.notes: Mass flow = linear fit to discharged mass from 0.05 s after opening to the end of the run. Beverloo: W = C rho_b sqrt(g) (D0 - k d)^2.5 with C = 0.58, d = 0.425 mm, rho_b from the poured packing fraction of dem-liggghts-tap.

dem-liggghts-tap.method: poured (apparent) and tapped density, laterally periodic column, 3 mm taps
dem-liggghts-tap.notes: 30 taps only (ASTM B527 uses up to 3000); the tapped value is the mean of the last 5 taps. Packing fraction in a slab 1 mm above the floor to 1 mm below the free surface; no side walls (periodic).

dem-liggghts-shear.method: plane (unrolled Schulze ring) shear cell: pre-shear at 200 Pa, shear to failure at 50/100/150 Pa
dem-liggghts-shear.notes: Real-size salt, E = 2e5 Pa, so normal stresses are kept at 50-200 Pa (overlaps < ~3 % of d); this is the stress range of a few mm to cm of powder head, i.e. the doser's, far below FT4/Schulze test stresses (kPa). Gravity off during shearing. ffc from Mohr circles on a straight yield locus through the three peak points.

dem-liggghts-spread.method: blade recoating, gap 2.5 mean diameters (1.06 mm), 50 mm/s, y-periodic 4.25 mm slice
dem-liggghts-spread.notes: Measured over x = 12-32 mm in 2 mm bins. Layer packing fraction = grain volume inside 0<z<gap / (bin area x gap). Coverage = projected area of grains whose centre is below the gap / bin area.

dem-liggghts-capillary.method: angle of repose (dem-liggghts-aor setup) with liquid-bridge cohesion, dry vs two liquid contents
dem-liggghts-capillary.notes: Dry baseline = the dry run of dem-liggghts-aor (identical setup). Liquid: surface tension 0.072 N/m, viscosity 1 mPa s, contact angle 20 deg, bridge rupture at 1.1 x contact distance (maxSeparationDistanceRatio), min separation ratio 1.01; grain-wall contacts dry.

dem-lammps-shear-mui.method: DEM periodic simple shear (Lees-Edwards) at constant normal stress -> mu(I), cohesive yield line
dem-lammps-shear-mui.notes: Non-cohesive: full stage list ran. JKR (gamma 8.5 mJ/m^2, Bo_g ~10) ran with a reduced stage list and mass_velocity damping (first attempt failed: 'Cannot use tsuji model with a cohesive normal model, jkr'). JKR 25 Pa stage did not reach its target (Pyy 34 Pa, still dilating): transient point. Pyy held by change_box feedback because fix press/berendsen refuses triclinic boxes. E reduced to 2e5 Pa as in the PR #180 twin.

dem-lammps-charge.method: DEM pour of unipolar tribocharged grains beside an oppositely charged wall (coul/cut)
dem-lammps-charge.code: LAMMPS (GRANULAR + coul/cut, atom_style hybrid sphere charge)
dem-lammps-charge.notes: 800 mobile grains + 300 frozen charged wall spheres. q/m values: 0, -1e-5 (task-brief range), -1e-4 C/kg (near the 1.7e-4 C/kg Gauss limit of a 0.425 mm grain); wall sigma 1e-5 C/m^2 (assumed, below the 2.7e-5 C/m^2 breakdown limit). coul/cut 1.2 mm, no image charges, fixed charges.

dem-yade-capillary.method: DEM column collapse of coarse-grained salt with pendular liquid bridges (Willett 2000 capillary force), dry vs two liquid contents
dem-yade-capillary.notes: Ran as intended at reduced scale (diameters coarse-grained x4, N=1200, 0.4 s after release). Marked partial because the dry baseline has no rolling resistance on a smooth floor and spreads into a monolayer, so no repose angle could be measured. The trend with liquid content is clear, but the dry-to-wet contrast is larger than real salt would show. Yade's ViscEl rolling resistance is viscous as coded (M = -mR*|Fn|*omega_rel), so mR was set to 0. Only the W=1% case was at rest at the 0.4 s cap; the dry runout is a lower bound (grains still rolling), and W=0.1% was still creeping (KE 8e-7 J).

dem-yade-directshear.method: DEM periodic triaxial compression with cohesive-frictional (brittle, re-forming) contacts at 3 confining stresses and 2 Bond numbers; Mohr-Coulomb fits of peak and residual states
dem-yade-directshear.notes: Real salt size (no coarse-graining), E=2e5 Pa, mu=0.5, etaRoll=0.3, sigma3 = 50/150/400 Pa (doser-hopper range), I=2.5e-3. Neither Bo=5 nor Bo=50 gives a Mohr-Coulomb cohesion intercept that stands out from the scatter (|c| < 20 Pa at N=600): the brittle bonds break as soon as a contact slides, and at Bo=50 the cohesion mainly loosens the compacted packing (solid fraction 0.571 vs 0.635 at 50 Pa), which lowers the peak. wall_s includes an earlier 3-run set compacted with mu=0.1 (looser samples; peak phi 41.5 deg, c -1.6 Pa).

dem-mercurydpm.method: DEM flat-bottomed silo discharge through a circular orifice vs Beverloo
dem-mercurydpm.notes: github.com/MercuryDPM/MercuryDPM does not exist (HTTP 404; git clone asked for credentials); cloned the official Bitbucket repo instead. Library + one demo built with make -j2 in 185 s. Grains coarse-grained x4 (1.44-1.96 mm). Linear spring-dashpot, tc = 1 ms, dt = tc_min/25. First attempt (tc/50, 0.9 s) was stopped as too slow for the 8 min budget. Status 'partial' = ran at reduced scale (coarse-grained x4, 2500-3000 grains, sub-second discharge windows). D=10 mm (D/d 5.9) clogged; D=14 mm (D/d 8.2) flowed at 0.84 x Beverloo.

dem-chrono-cpu.method: DEM silo discharge through a square orifice at four sizes, with a Beverloo fit
dem-chrono-cpu.code: Project Chrono / PyChrono core ChSystemSMC (Hertz, MultiStep tangential), Bullet collision, CPU, 1 thread
dem-chrono-cpu.notes: Coarse-grained 4x (mean d 1.70 mm), E=2e5 Pa, 16 mm silo, 0.2 s settle + 0.6 s discharge per orifice. Bullet with SI (metre) units blew up (grains ejected at about 700 m/s within 0.02 s, as PR #180 also saw), so Chrono runs internally in millimetres. SetRollingFriction has no effect in core ChSystemSMC (identical rolling-sphere speed with mu_roll 0 and 0.3). The L=5.5 mm (L/d=3.2) flow was slow and intermittent, near jamming.

dem-tribocharge-numba.method: Self-written quasi-2D DEM (numba) of salt in a rotating PLA tube cross-section with condenser-model contact charging, Coulomb + image forces, gas-breakdown charge caps (air vs dry argon)
dem-tribocharge-numba.notes: Quasi-2D monolayer, 600 grains, soft contacts (k_n = 5 N/m), no grain rotation, no humidity leakage. Wall counter-charge capped at the same breakdown density over patch area (arc x one grain diameter); this wall capacity, not the per-grain cap, limits q/m. No time compression (K_ACC = 1).

mpm-taichi.method: Material Point Method (MLS-MPM) with Drucker-Prager elastoplasticity (Klar et al. 2016)
mpm-taichi.notes: 2D plane strain, per metre depth; rho_bulk 1250 kg/m3 assumed; E=0.3 MPa (soft for speed); no grain size in the continuum, so the k*d term becomes a grid-scale offset. Resolution check: 12 mm slot on a 256^2 grid gives W = 4.46 kg/(m s) vs 2.02 on 128^2 (Beverloo C=1.03: 5.30), so low W at small D/dx is mostly a resolution artefact.

sph-granular.method: SPH, elastic-perfectly plastic Drucker-Prager (Bui et al. 2008 type), 2D plane strain
sph-granular.code: self-written numba SPH (run.py); PySPH 1.0b2 installed but has no granular/Drucker-Prager scheme
sph-granular.version: numba 0.68.1, numpy 2.5.4, python 3.12 (PySPH 1.0b2 built from PyPI sdist in a separate venv)
sph-granular.notes: First attempt with artificial viscosity alpha=0.1 blew up at t=0.02 s (particles ejected at 10 m/s); final runs use alpha=0.5. PySPH 1.0b2 built from the PyPI sdist (about 5 min) and its stock elliptical_drop example ran (exit 0, 5025 particles, setup 11.7 s, run 4.3 s), but PySPH has no granular/Drucker-Prager scheme, so the granular runs use the self-written numba code.

fem-druckerprager.method: 2D plane-strain small-strain elastoplastic FEM, associated Drucker-Prager (Mohr-Coulomb plane-strain match), trapdoor/arching collapse by gravity increase
fem-druckerprager.code: self-written numpy/scipy FEM (run.py): Q8 serendipity, 2x2 reduced integration, closed-form DP return mapping, modified Newton with factorised elastic stiffness
fem-druckerprager.notes: Collapse = no convergence (residual 1e-4) within 800 modified-Newton iterations, bracketed by 4 bisections; sigma1 = 400 Pa is an assumed consolidation stress taken from the Janssen estimate in analytic-orifice-screw.

mui-rheology.method: local mu(I) rheology (Jop et al. 2006) and non-local granular fluidity (Henann & Kamrin 2013; dynamic form, Kamrin & Henann 2015) for inclined-plane flow
mui-rheology.notes: Glass-bead parameters (d=0.5 mm): mu_s=tan20.9, mu_2=tan32.76, I0=0.279, b=(mu_2-mu_s)/I0, A=0.48, phi=0.6. NGF BCs: g=0 at rough base, dg/dz=0 at free surface. Timings: {"local_transient_s": 40.1, "ngf_hstop_bisection_s": 49.3, "ngf_phase_check_s": 2.1, "ngf_profiles_flowrule_s": 0.3}

analytic-orifice-screw.method: Beverloo/Hagen-type orifice discharge, Jenike arching, Janssen, screw volumetric model

fill_law_A_fit.form: m = a + b sin(tilt) [mg/rev] == rho_b V_p (phi0 + phi1 sin tilt)

analytic-orifice-screw.notes: Closed-form models; fill laws A and B have 2 parameters each fitted to the 4 measured points (stated, with residuals). Outlet-limited curve and all Beverloo/Jenike/Janssen numbers are not fitted.

ca-avalanche.method: cellular automata: 1D Oslo rice pile (avalanche statistics, self-organised slope) and a tilted-feeder outflow CA with a cohesion-like start/stop threshold gap (I_stop, afterflow)
ca-avalanche.notes: Lattice toy models: lengths in sites/cells, mass in parcels. Timings: {"oslo_s": 72.6, "feeder_scan_s": 33.2, "feeder_kscan_s": 44.0, "animation_s": 31.9} Feeder rule: only a column that itself toppled is 'moving' (needs s_f) for 3 sweeps; an earlier version that also activated neighbours made c irrelevant and was discarded. I_stop ~ 1 - inflow/mean burst in incremental mode, so absolute I_stop depends on parcel size; trends with c, tilt and drive rate are the result.

mc-packing.method: Monte Carlo / geometric sphere packing: random sequential addition, sequential drop-and-roll deposition (Visscher-Bolsterli / Jullien-Meakin) with a stick-probability cohesion proxy, force-biased (FIRE overlap-removal) compression

key_results.units: packing fraction phi (solid volume / total volume), dimensionless

mc-packing.notes: 3D, periodic in x-y (deposition: flat floor, phi measured in a bulk slab 3 d_max above the floor to 2 d_max below the 10th-percentile surface height; RSA and compression: fully periodic cube). Geometric packings are scale-free, so NaCl vs AlSi10Mg differ only through PSD shape; cohesion enters only through p_stick. Monodisperse runs are validation against literature.

moisture-sorption.method: GAB isotherm + Fickian vapour diffusion + Kelvin brine bridges + Rabinovich capillary force -> Bond number -> Rumpf/Mohr-Coulomb/Jenike flow prediction

moisture-sorption.notes: Many inputs are assumed (GAB C, K; asperity height and radius; Hamaker constant; coordination; boundary layer; wicking above DRH; BaCl2.2H2O DRH and brine surface tension). See README.

bayes-grainlearning.method: Iterative Bayesian filtering (sequential Monte Carlo + GMM resampling) calibrating (mu_s, Bo) of a stand-in doser model against measured salt mg/rev vs tilt
bayes-grainlearning.notes: Forward model is a stand-in (screw push + Beverloo annulus + tilt threshold), not DEM. GrainLearning's likelihood uses a relative (obs-scaled) Gaussian whose width sigma is tuned each iteration to an effective sample size of 0.3, so the posterior width reflects that annealing scheme rather than the measurement error bars.

bayes-gp-emulator-mcmc.method: Gaussian-process emulator on a 48-point Sobol design over (mu_s, mu_r, Bo) of a stand-in doser model + emcee posterior; identifiability with and without an angle-of-repose observable

equivalent_DEM_cost.note: 48 parameter sets x 4 tilts, one 30-CPU-min revolution each

bayes-gp-emulator-mcmc.notes: Forward model is a stand-in (screw push + Beverloo annulus + tilt threshold; Zhou-form AoR), not DEM. The AoR observation is synthetic (stand-in evaluated at the DEM twin's nominal set mu_s=0.5, mu_r=0.3, Bo=0, sd 1.5 deg); the wall-friction observation is also synthetic (mu_w = 0.4 +/- 0.04, model mu_w = 0.8 mu_s). GP predictive variance is added to the likelihood variance.

gns-gnn-simulator.method: Learned graph-network simulator (GNS, Sanchez-Gonzalez et al. 2020; Kumar & Vantassel 2023) trained on a self-generated 2D numba-DEM granular column-collapse dataset; rollout vs DEM on held-out columns
gns-gnn-simulator.code: geoelements/gns LearnedSimulator (own training loop with the gns loss/noise) + self-written numba DEM

key_results.route: self-generated dataset (no small pretrained 2D sand GNS model available; gns-sample has only WaterDropSample data, no checkpoint)

gns-gnn-simulator.notes: Reduced GNS (5 message-passing steps, latent 64) trained ~5000 steps on 1 CPU thread, versus ~1e6+ steps in the papers. Rollouts track the DEM for the two in-range columns (runout within -6 % and +20 % of the DEM runout distance) and blow up for the taller, out-of-range column (test_1, H/W 2.6).

cfd-dem.method: coupled CFD-DEM (unresolved, volume-averaged gas + soft-sphere DEM, two-way momentum coupling)
cfd-dem.code: OpenFOAM DPMFoam (MFiX attempted: not installable from public conda channels)

key_results.arrival_definition: first crossing of y = 3 mm (plug released at y = 31 mm); output every 2 ms

cfd-dem.notes: Reduced scale: AlSi10Mg coarse-grained 35->100 um, 846 particles, E=1e4 Pa, 0.13 s. MFiX failed: PackagesNotFoundInChannelsError for 'mfix' on conda-forge/mfix channels. One-way reference has contacts off (DPM).

contact-dynamics.method: non-smooth contact dynamics (Moreau-Jean, NLGS), 2D rigid discs, flat-bottomed silo discharge vs outlet width
contact-dynamics.notes: 2D, 600 discs (d_mean = 1 mm, scale-free in NSCD), dt=2e-4 s, 1.2 s per width; build ~11 min. No pip/conda package: source build; np.cross 2-vector shim for NumPy 2.5.

dem-fem-coupling.method: two-way partitioned DEM-FEM coupling (4C PASI): DEM grains falling onto a clamped nonlinear neo-Hookean membrane
dem-fem-coupling.code: 4C (open-source successor of BACI), Docker image ghcr.io/4c-multiphysics/4c:main
dem-fem-coupling.notes: 4 earlier attempts with Aitken relaxation/tight tolerances aborted at impact with 'The partitioned PASI solver did not converge in ITEMAX steps!'; final run uses fixed relaxation 0.5, disp tol 1e-5 m, IGNORE_CONV_CHECK.

dem-nonspherical.method: non-spherical DEM: 8-sphere rigid clumps (rounded cubes) vs spheres with/without rolling resistance; lifted-cylinder heap

key_results.liggghts_superquadric: atom_style superquadric present but no fix nve/superquadric or particletemplate/superquadric -> not runnable; multisphere styles present

dem-nonspherical.notes: Reduced scale (361 particles/heap, heaps 4-6 grains tall); two seeds; AoR estimates noisy (up to 7-11 deg seed-to-seed). wall_s = in-script time of the six main-set runs.

surrogate-pinn.method: Physics-informed neural networks for the Janssen powder-column stress: parametric forward surrogate over K*mu_w and inverse inference of K*mu_w from noisy stress readings
surrogate-pinn.notes: Janssen ODE is a 1D continuum stand-in for the hopper/inlet stress, not a doser model; the PINN is compared with the closed-form solution and with a least-squares fit of that solution to the same data.
